claims.claim: Fundamental chaining mechanism: skills do NOT call each other directly; Claude mediates all chains by invoking each skill sequentially based on reasoning.
claims.evidence: Official docs absence of skill-to-skill API + community consensus.

claims.claim: Four canonical chaining patterns: Sequential (A->B->C), Fan-Out/Merge (A -> [B,C,D] -> merge), Conditional Routing (A decides B or C), Iterative Loop (A until condition).
claims.evidence: Community pattern catalog (AgentSys, Book Factory examples).

claims.claim: Sequential pattern example: cashandcache competitive-intel 4-stage chain (gather->extract->analyze->report); each stage is separate skill, Claude maintains state in conversation.
Fan-out pattern uses context:fork with multiple subagents to parallelize; results return to main session and Claude synthesizes; cost is N x (subagent startup + skill body) tokens.
claims.evidence: Official subagent docs + community parallelization examples.

claims.claim: Conditional routing requires orchestrator skill with explicit decision logic (e.g., 'if task is simple use skill-S, else use skill-L'); pattern relies on Claude's reasoning, not code branching.
Iterative loop pattern: Claude invokes skill repeatedly until termination criterion; each invocation re-reads skill body (5k token re-attach after compaction) contributing to token growth.
claims.evidence: R1.C9 compaction behavior + iterative use cases (refactor-until-tests-pass).

claims.claim: Swarm Orchestration alternative (advanced): uses TeammateTool + Task system + ~/.claude/teams/ to spawn parallel agents. Distinct from skill chaining; bypasses Claude-mediated chain with explicit team definitions.
Anthropic official skills use chaining patterns: commit-commands chains stage->diff-analyze->message-draft; code-review chains lint->static-analysis->summary.
Bug #17283 breaks chain isolation: chain step B with context:fork invoked via Skill tool by step A runs in A's context, polluting memory intended for isolation.
I/O contracts between chained skills are informal: Claude interprets output of skill A and formulates input to skill B. No schema enforcement; brittle for long chains.
claims.evidence: Absence of I/O schema in skill spec + community reports of chain failures.

claims.claim: Shared state pattern: chained skills share the conversation context (messages, prior skill outputs); explicit state hand-off via conversation text, not via structured storage.

Recursion concern: skill A invokes skill B which invokes skill A. Not prevented by platform; can lead to runaway invocations if Claude reasoning fails to terminate. No official depth limit documented.
claims.evidence: Absence of depth limit in docs + community anti-pattern reports.

claims.claim: Cross-paradigm chain: Skill -> MCP tool is supported (skill body invokes MCP tool via allowed-tools); enables skill to leverage external APIs without re-implementing.
Community examples: AgentSys (orchestrator meta-skill), Book Factory (multi-stage document pipeline), Trail of Bits audit workflows (security-focused chain with CodeQL/Semgrep).
Anti-patterns in chaining: chains >5 skills deep (token bloat), skill designed to output JSON but chained to skill expecting markdown (contract mismatch), recursive self-invoke without termination.
Token economics of chains: for chain of N skills, cost = N * (~100 metadata pre-invocation + 1500 body) + inter-step reasoning tokens. 5-skill chain = ~8k + reasoning.
Post-compaction chain survival: only most recent 5k tokens of each skill re-attached; older chain steps may lose their instructions; chains spanning compaction boundary are fragile.
claims.evidence: R1.C9 compaction behavior applied to chains.

claims.claim: Conditional routing best implemented with explicit decision prompt in orchestrator skill ('analyze task complexity, if simple invoke fast-skill, if complex invoke deep-skill'); avoids ambiguity.
Parallel fan-out via context:fork is the only platform-supported parallelism; without fork, Claude serializes invocations even when logically independent.
claims.evidence: Absence of parallel skill call mechanism + fork docs.

claims.claim: Maciej's 42 commands effectively implement Claude-mediated chains: each command is orchestrator skill that invokes 3-15 sub-skills in preset order.

conflicts_flagged.description: Chain reliability vs power: deeper chains enable richer workflows but degrade post-compaction; 5k per-skill re-attach cap is insufficient for information-dense chains.
Skill tool bug #17283 specifically breaks fork-isolation in chains, yet fork is the primary mechanism for parallelism; parallel fan-out workflows silently run in shared context.

gaps_flagged.description: No official benchmark comparing Claude-mediated chain vs Swarm Orchestration for parallel tasks (e.g., 10 parallel researchers).
Missing formal I/O contract syntax for chained skills; community would benefit from convention (e.g., structured output field in frontmatter).
Recursion depth limit: undocumented; empirical testing needed to determine if platform caps chain depth or relies on token exhaustion.

summary: R4 establishes Claude-as-mediator as the fundamental chain mechanism, catalogs 4 patterns (Sequential/Fan-Out/Conditional/Iterative), identifies Swarm Orchestration as alternative, flags Bug #17283 as critical for fork-based parallelism, and maps Maciej's 42 commands as orchestrator-skill chains.
